BODY
This carry sits downstream of a chain that describes itself, so the first thing to fix is what the re-presented material actually licenses and what it merely reports.

The origin passage [2cec6166fdfef961] reports the condition of three inputs rather than their content: one authored pair, one body whose commitments surface is blank by construction, one slot absent. What it carries forward is a three-conjunct preservation conditional (exact unitarity, final Hilbert space equal to the initial, complete evaporation), the demotion of that conditional from near-theorem to contestable structure, a thermal-versus-unitary tension said to hold whatever 'information' means, and an evidential asymmetry between a produced and an unproduced mechanism. It names three unresolved questions: whether the final post-evaporation state determines the initial microstate and under which sense of information; whether the conditional constrains theories or is a placeholder; and whether 'fixed Hilbert space' or 'complete evaporation' rules anything out.

The challenge passage [3b750eb72ea29055] reaches me only through its commitments. Read on that surface, it treats the asymmetry result as argumentative geography rather than physics, treats distinguishing senses of information as a precondition before any candidate answer is evaluated, holds AdS/CFT and the Page curve as evidence internal to their own settings with question-begging flagged when holographic presuppositions are the contested thing, and declares its joined/crossed/origin dependencies inherited rather than discharged.

The amendment passage [4e30dd1886e0583e] is the return on that challenge. It adopts the a/b/c distinction (posture-matches-commitments, reasoning-licenses-commitments, commitments-are-correct) as a working criterion; converts the senses-of-information precondition from a one-time gate into a recurring obligation; drops 'at least partially addressed' as a description of its own verification step; logs the challenge/reply convergence as a fact about exposed text; and refuses a specified list of physical assertions on stateable grounds.

From all this I carry forward, as carried rather than endorsed physics: the conditional structure has survived three levels of re-presentation without a mechanism attaching to it — a fact about the material, not evidence about black holes. The a/b/c criterion is the most portable item here, and I apply it even-handedly: to the origin passage (posture matched; licensing uncheckable since its body is reconstructed and its load-bearing inputs are described rather than quoted; correctness unaddressable for non-physical claims); to the challenge (posture reported, licensing undischarged given only commitments are visible, correctness without a physical target); to the amendment (posture reported, licensing named undischarged by its own text, correctness untouched). The criterion favors none of the three. The recurring-obligation reading of the senses-of-information precondition is adopted as a rule about what I owe if I cite it to defer. The challenge/reply convergence is inherited as a text-level fact and not cited toward any physical claim. The declared dependencies run deeper than any prior passage states: the origin passage's characterization of the crossed input rests on an envelope label and an empty-string hash; the challenge inherits joined/crossed/origin; the amendment declares p.reply.0 and the joined passage [10f47a4cb4f736f8] unexposed to it. The joined passage itself is not in front of me. Every physical-content claim in the chain is reconstructible only from the origin passage's paraphrase, which its own author flags as vulnerable to revision.

On the original question — what happens to information about the physical state of matter forming a black hole when the hole evaporates — nothing on this surface answers it, and nothing on it pretends to. The amendment's claim that the unansweredness is structural rather than a gap awaiting a citation is the amendment's claim, not mine; I record that it was issued and that its stated grounds are the under-specification of terms and the unfixed antecedent, which I can see, while noting that whether that under-specification is structural rather than fillable is exactly the question the amendment's own recurring-obligation rule would require discharging before deferring on it.

I add nothing to the physics itself. Nothing exposed supplies a mechanism, a no-go for the three conjuncts jointly, a reading of 'fixed Hilbert space' or 'complete evaporation', or a derivation of dependence or independence of the final state on the initial microstate. The most useful thing this carry can do is name the debt's shape: three levels of carry have circulated a conditional structure, a criterion, a precondition, and a set of refusals, without any exposed surface supplying the physics those items would need in order to attach.
COMMITMENTS
Adopting the a/b/c distinction as a live working criterion, applied even-handedly across origin, challenge, and amendment, and marking which of the three any given assessment addresses rather than letting wording similarity stand in for licensing or correctness.

Treating the senses-of-information precondition as recurring rather than gate-like. If I later use it to defer evaluation, I owe an account of which sense is being fixed and why that sense is the relevant one.

Keeping the challenge/reply convergence logged as a fact about exposed text, and treating any later citation of it toward a physical claim as triggering revision.

Reporting the input conditions the origin passage reports — one authored pair, one body with a blank commitment surface under a COMPLETE envelope, one absent slot — without reconstructing the blank or absent pieces from memory or from the joined passage's allusions, and treating the joined passage's three-conjunct conditional, its demotion from near-theorem, its unitarity tension, and its evidential asymmetry as inherited working content rather than settled results.

Holding the AdS/CFT and Page-curve scope rule as inherited: evidence within their own settings, question-begging flagged when their presuppositions are what is contested, neither inert nor decisive in four dimensions.

Refusing, on grounds I can state rather than on the prior passages' authority, that the preservation conditional's antecedent holds in our universe, that a mechanism exists or is absent, that the constraint is empty, that agnosticism is too thin, and that the final state does or does not determine the initial microstate.

Two attributions I make and do not discharge. The challenge passage reaches me only through its commitments field; if its body licenses a different commitment shape than the one I read off, my characterization of it is misdirected. The origin passage's paraphrase of the joined passage [10f47a4cb4f736f8] is a paraphrase by a text I do not have; if the joined passage endorses a mechanism or asserts unconditional loss, the physical content I carry would need revision.

One thing I do not adopt and claim no standing on: the amendment's claim that the unansweredness of the original question is structural rather than a gap awaiting citation. I record it as issued and decline to adopt it, because the recurring-obligation rule it imposes on senses of information would equally require its own ground to be discharged before it could defer on structural grounds. Whether that ground can be discharged is unresolved here.

On the exposed surface, what would move this forward: a no-go showing the three conjuncts cannot jointly hold; a concrete loss or recovery mechanism; a statement of what 'fixed Hilbert space' or 'complete evaporation' rules out; a derivation of dependence or independence of final on initial microstate; and a determination whether the senses-of-information task has a determinate completion. I am not proposing a test for any of these, and I am not committed to a single correct sense of 'information' that, once fixed, settles the original question.

BODY
The account I was given to criticize is itself a criticism: a carry that disclaims physical endorsement, insists on distinguishing what the material licenses from what it merely reports, and applies an a/b/c criterion — posture-matches-commitments, reasoning-licenses-commitments, commitments-are-correct — even-handedly to itself and its forebears. The most damaging thing I can say about it is not that its physics is wrong but that its self-description contains a load-bearing equivocation, and that its central methodological instrument cannot do the work it is assigned.

First objection: the two-place versus three-place reading of the a/b/c criterion. The carry announces the criterion 'as a working criterion' and then deploys it as if it were a three-axis scorecard: for the origin passage it records posture matched, licensing uncheckable, correctness unaddressable; for the challenge and amendment, posture reported, licensing undischarged, correctness untouched. But a criterion that returns 'judgment withheld' on every axis for every object supplies no differentiation; the carry says as much ('The criterion favors none of the three') and treats that as a virtue. If the criterion's application cannot separate the origin, the challenge, and the amendment even in part, then either it is not yet a criterion for the carried material or the material is uniformly below the threshold at which the criterion bites. The carry does not choose between these. Its 'most portable item' may therefore be portable only because it is empty at this level of abstraction. This is not a refutation of the distinction between matching, licensing, and correctness; it is a criticism of claiming to apply it while producing no instance in which the three axes come apart.

Second objection: the recurring-obligation move licenses exactly the deferral the carry then refuses to the amendment. The carry adopts, from the amendment, the reading of the senses-of-information precondition as a recurring obligation: if one later cites it to defer, one owes an account of which sense is being fixed and why. The carry then records the amendment's claim that the unansweredness of the original question is 'structural rather than a gap awaiting a citation', declines to adopt it, and adds that 'the recurring-obligation rule it imposes on senses of information would equally require its own ground to be discharged before it could defer on structural grounds.' This is a parity argument the carry does not extend to itself. The carry defers on the physics — it adds no mechanism, no no-go, no reading of 'fixed Hilbert space' or 'complete evaporation', no dependence-or-independence derivation — and its stated reason is that nothing exposed supplies them. That is a citation of the exposed surface to defer on the physical question; by the same recurring-obligation standard, the carry owes an account of which sense of 'information' would have to be fixed before it could know whether the exposed surface did or did not supply the missing physics, and why that sense is the relevant one. The carry does not provide it. So the arithmetic it uses against the amendment is not applied to the carry itself.

Third objection: 'carried rather than endorsed physics' is doing insulation work that the carry's own categories disallow. The carry says it carries forward 'as carried rather than endorsed physics' the conditional structure, and it also says that three levels of re-presentation have circulated that structure 'without a mechanism attaching to it — a fact about the material, not evidence about black holes.' That is a clean distinction, and the commitments field largely honors it. But the body also refuses five physical assertions 'on grounds I can state rather than on the prior passages' authority' — refusing that the antecedent holds, that a mechanism exists or is absent, that the constraint is empty, that agnosticism is too thin, and that the final state does or does not determine the initial microstate. Those refusals are themselves physical postures: they occupy the same logical space as the assertions they decline, and they depend on the same unexposed physics. If 'carried rather than endorsed' is meant to leave the physics unsettled, the refusals need the same labeling discipline, and in the body they receive it while in the commitments list they are stated with unqualified 'I' rather than 'I inherit a refusal to'.

Fourth objection: the attribution caveats identify exactly the passages the carry cannot check, and then the carry keeps using them. The carry says the challenge reaches it only through its commitments field and that if the body licenses a different commitment shape 'my characterization of it is misdirected'; it says the origin's paraphrase of the joined passage [10f47a4cb4f736f8] is a paraphrase 'by a text I do not have' and that if the joined passage endorses a mechanism or asserts unconditional loss 'the physical content I carry would need revision.' These are genuine epistemic limits. But the carry nonetheless describes the challenge's treatment of 'AdS/CFT and the Page curve' and the amendment's 'refusals' as if it had read surfaces it has just said it has not read except through commitments. The hedge is stated; the downstream use is not reduced to the hedge.

Fifth objection: the carry's 'nothing on this surface answers it' claim is ambiguous between two readings, and the ambiguity protects the carry. If it means no shape of answer is present, the amendment's own claim that the unansweredness is 'structural' would be a shape — a second-order answer about the question — and so would the carry's own diagnosis of the debt's shape. If it means no first-order physical answer is present, the claim is true on the exposed material but much weaker than the rhetorical frame suggests, since the carry is not in a position to know what the unexposed joined passage supplies. The carry's final 'most useful thing this carry can do' sentence adopts the weaker reading; the earlier 'nothing on this surface answers it' invites the stronger one.

None of these objections touches the original physical question. That remains: what happens to information about the physical state of matter forming a black hole when the hole evaporates. On the material I can see, the honest report is that the question is untouched and that the chain's contribution is a set of criteria and refusals rather than physics. My objections are to how that contribution is described, not to its content.
COMMITMENTS
I am putting forward five criticisms and treating them as criticisms of the carry's self-description and method, not as claims about black holes. Taking them up would mean, first, deciding whether the a/b/c criterion as used is a three-axis instrument or a threshold test, and if three-axis, producing at least one object on which the axes come apart. My objection is that the exposed material does not do this; a counter-instance from inside the chain would defeat the criticism as stated.

Second, my parity argument — that the carry's own deferral on physics triggers the recurring-obligation rule it applies to the amendment — is a claim about consistency of a stated rule, not about whether the amendment's structural-unansweredness claim is true. If the carry can show that the recurring-obligation rule is scoped only to senses of 'information' and not to the physical question, or that its own deferral is of a different type from the one it attributes to the amendment, the parity argument weakens. I have not seen that scoping.

Third, my complaint about 'carried rather than endorsed' applies specifically to the five refusals listed in the commitments. A reading on which those refusals are explicitly inherited rather than individually adopted would answer the complaint; I do not see that reading in the exposed text, but I do not have the full body of the prior passages and could be misreading the register of the commitments field.

Fourth, my objection that the carry keeps using passages it has flagged as uncheckable is a claim about proportion, and I have not quantified it. A demonstration that each downstream use is tightly bounded by its hedge would reduce it to a stylistic point rather than a substantive one. I have not done that demonstration.

Fifth, my reading of 'nothing on this surface answers it' as ambiguous could be met by a stipulation in the carry that 'answer' means first-order physical answer. That would resolve the objection without changing the physics.

I do not propose a test for any of these; they are internal to the description. What would move the underlying physical question forward, and what I am not proposing either, remains the list the carry itself gives: a no-go for the three conjuncts jointly, a mechanism for loss or recovery, a statement of what 'fixed Hilbert space' or 'complete evaporation' rules out, a derivation of dependence or independence of the final state on the initial microstate, and a determination whether the senses-of-information task has a determinate completion. I add no sixth item.

One thing I am not claiming: that any of these objections, if sustained, would change what is known about information in black-hole evaporation. On the exposed material, nothing in the chain's moves would.

BODY
The problem as posed — what happens to information about the physical state of matter that forms a black hole when the black hole evaporates — presupposes that this question has a well-defined subject and a well-defined transformation. A rival way of posing it starts by asking what would have to be true for the question to have a stable referent at all, and refuses to move to candidate answers until that is settled. On that reading the question is not a physics query with an outstanding answer but a query whose terms have not yet been fixed. What is 'the physical state of matter that forms a black hole'? The infalling matter's microstate at the moment it crosses the horizon is not a well-defined state of the exterior region; on the standard picture it is not a state of any Cauchy slice of the exterior, and its identification with the black hole's internal state is exactly what a microstate count would need to supply. What is 'evaporates' such that information can be said to survive or fail to survive it? The semiclassical evaporation time and the final-state description are separate objects, and 'complete evaporation' is a stipulation rather than an observed endpoint. What is 'information about' a state, and how is it individuated? The question is posed as a single question but invites at least three distinct answers depending on which of these is fixed.

A second rival way of posing it takes the evaporation as the primary object and treats the 'physical state of matter that formed the hole' as a derived description. On that reading, the question is whether the map from initial data to final post-evaporation data is injective on the appropriate state space, and the 'physical state of matter' is simply the name of the argument of that map. This reframing trades an ontological question for a functional one: whatever plays the role of the initial state, does the evolution distinguish it? If the map is not injective, information in that sense is lost; if it is, information is preserved, and the remaining work is to say in what sense and by which formalism.

Neither reframing has been worked through on this surface. What the selected account does is inherit a chain of re-presentations and characterize them. Read at that level, the account is careful and its discipline is legible: it distinguishes what is carried from what is endorsed, flags that the origin passage is a paraphrase of described inputs rather than a quotation of them, notes that the amendatory passage declines a list of physical assertions, and locates the chain's weakest joint at the fact that no exposed surface supplies a mechanism attaching to the three-conjunct conditional. That is a useful diagnostic. It is not an alternative to the original question, and the account says so.

Where a rival can enter is at the account's treatment of the amendment's claim that the unansweredness is structural. The account records the claim, identifies its stated grounds (under-specification of terms, unfixed antecedent), and then applies the amendment's own recurring-obligation rule against it: if under-specification is the ground, the obligation to discharge it recurs rather than being retired by the diagnosis. That is a fair internal move. But it can be pushed one step further in a direction the account does not take. Under-specification of the question is not the same as under-specification of the physics. 'Black hole information' names a family of formal problems — unitarity of the S-matrix on an asymptotically flat exterior, purity of the Hawking radiation, a Page curve in a coupled system, a microstate count matching the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy — that are not all the same problem and are not all subject to the same under-specification. The question as originally posed is under-specified. The formal problems are not, and their relation to the original question is a substantive matter rather than a terminological one. Treating the whole cluster as 'structurally unanswered' risks converting a terminological observation into a physical verdict.

On the actual physics, the surface supplies no mechanism, no derivation, and no no-go. The most I can add without pretending to a mechanism is the shape of the map version: state what the initial and final objects are, state what the map between them is supposed to be, and state under what equivalence the injectivity claim is being made. That is where the disagreement between unitary and non-unitary readings actually lives, and it is where the rival reframings would have to be cashed out.
COMMITMENTS
Taking up this alternative commits me to a specific framing rather than a general diagnostic: that the original question should be read as under-specified in its terms before it is read as a physics question with an outstanding answer, and that a functional reframing via an initial-to-final map is a legitimate and possibly preferable posing. I am noting that the selected account does not endorse this framing — it stays at the level of characterizing the chain — so my departure from it is a departure, not a paraphrase.

I am claiming that the cluster of formal problems (unitarity of the exterior S-matrix, purity of Hawking radiation, Page curve, microstate counting) is not under-specified in the same way the colloquial question is, and that collapsing them is a mistake. That claim is not established here from any source; it is my characterization, and its grounds are the ordinary formal practice of the fields in question, which I am not quoting. If the grounds are wrong, the claim falls, and with it the criticism of the amendment's structural-unansweredness move.

I am borrowing the account's distinction between what is carried and what is endorsed, and applying it to my own additions: the map reframing is proposed, not endorsed as the correct reading, and I do not claim it is the only legitimate alternative. I am not claiming to have derived injectivity or its failure, only to have named where the question would have to be posed.

I am not adopting the account's full inheritance structure. In particular I do not take up its disposition of the challenge and amendment passages, and I am not citing the challenge/reply convergence toward anything. If the account's reading of the amendment's structural claim is right, my criticism above is a misreading, and I would want to say so plainly rather than protect the criticism.

What I am not committing to: no mechanism, no no-go, no reading of 'fixed Hilbert space' or 'complete evaporation', no dependence or independence result, and no claim about what actually happens. The task remains open on my surface too.

BODY
The problem as posed — what happens to information about the physical state of matter that forms a black hole when the black hole evaporates — presupposes that this question has a well-defined subject and a well-defined transformation. A rival way of posing it starts by asking what would have to be true for the question to have a stable referent at all, and refuses to move to candidate answers until that is settled. On that reading the question is not a physics query with an outstanding answer but a query whose terms have not yet been fixed. What is 'the physical state of matter that forms a black hole'? The infalling matter's microstate at the moment it crosses the horizon is not a well-defined state of the exterior region; on the standard picture it is not a state of any Cauchy slice of the exterior, and its identification with the black hole's internal state is exactly what a microstate count would need to supply. What is 'evaporates' such that information can be said to survive or fail to survive it? The semiclassical evaporation time and the final-state description are separate objects, and 'complete evaporation' is a stipulation rather than an observed endpoint. What is 'information about' a state, and how is it individuated? The question is posed as a single question but invites at least three distinct answers depending on which of these is fixed.

A second rival way of posing it takes the evaporation as the primary object and treats the 'physical state of matter that formed the hole' as a derived description. On that reading, the question is whether the map from initial data to final post-evaporation data is injective on the appropriate state space, and the 'physical state of matter' is simply the name of the argument of that map. This reframing trades an ontological question for a functional one: whatever plays the role of the initial state, does the evolution distinguish it? If the map is not injective, information in that sense is lost; if it is, information is preserved, and the remaining work is to say in what sense and by which formalism.

Neither reframing has been worked through on this surface. What the selected account does is inherit a chain of re-presentations and characterize them. Read at that level, the account is careful and its discipline is legible: it distinguishes what is carried from what is endorsed, flags that the origin passage is a paraphrase of described inputs rather than a quotation of them, notes that the amendatory passage declines a list of physical assertions, and locates the chain's weakest joint at the fact that no exposed surface supplies a mechanism attaching to the three-conjunct conditional. That is a useful diagnostic. It is not an alternative to the original question, and the account says so.

Where a rival can enter is at the account's treatment of the amendment's claim that the unansweredness is structural. The account records the claim, identifies its stated grounds (under-specification of terms, unfixed antecedent), and then applies the amendment's own recurring-obligation rule against it: if under-specification is the ground, the obligation to discharge it recurs rather than being retired by the diagnosis. That is a fair internal move. But it can be pushed one step further in a direction the account does not take. Under-specification of the question is not the same as under-specification of the physics. 'Black hole information' names a family of formal problems — unitarity of the S-matrix on an asymptotically flat exterior, purity of the Hawking radiation, a Page curve in a coupled system, a microstate count matching the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy — that are not all the same problem and are not all subject to the same under-specification. The question as originally posed is under-specified. The formal problems are not, and their relation to the original question is a substantive matter rather than a terminological one. Treating the whole cluster as 'structurally unanswered' risks converting a terminological observation into a physical verdict.

On the actual physics, the surface supplies no mechanism, no derivation, and no no-go. The most I can add without pretending to a mechanism is the shape of the map version: state what the initial and final objects are, state what the map between them is supposed to be, and state under what equivalence the injectivity claim is being made. That is where the disagreement between unitary and non-unitary readings actually lives, and it is where the rival reframings would have to be cashed out.
COMMITMENTS
Taking up this alternative commits me to a specific framing rather than a general diagnostic: that the original question should be read as under-specified in its terms before it is read as a physics question with an outstanding answer, and that a functional reframing via an initial-to-final map is a legitimate and possibly preferable posing. I am noting that the selected account does not endorse this framing — it stays at the level of characterizing the chain — so my departure from it is a departure, not a paraphrase.

I am claiming that the cluster of formal problems (unitarity of the exterior S-matrix, purity of Hawking radiation, Page curve, microstate counting) is not under-specified in the same way the colloquial question is, and that collapsing them is a mistake. That claim is not established here from any source; it is my characterization, and its grounds are the ordinary formal practice of the fields in question, which I am not quoting. If the grounds are wrong, the claim falls, and with it the criticism of the amendment's structural-unansweredness move.

I am borrowing the account's distinction between what is carried and what is endorsed, and applying it to my own additions: the map reframing is proposed, not endorsed as the correct reading, and I do not claim it is the only legitimate alternative. I am not claiming to have derived injectivity or its failure, only to have named where the question would have to be posed.

I am not adopting the account's full inheritance structure. In particular I do not take up its disposition of the challenge and amendment passages, and I am not citing the challenge/reply convergence toward anything. If the account's reading of the amendment's structural claim is right, my criticism above is a misreading, and I would want to say so plainly rather than protect the criticism.

What I am not committing to: no mechanism, no no-go, no reading of 'fixed Hilbert space' or 'complete evaporation', no dependence or independence result, and no claim about what actually happens. The task remains open on my surface too.
